To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mutations in the ATP-binding cassette transporter subunit of the KATP channel cause ND and CHI and that the affinities of these mutants for ATP and ADPP are related to the clinical phenotypes.

(1) ND and CHI are associated with altered affinities for MgATP and MgADP; (2) the affinities of the ND mutants for MgATP are greater than those of the CHI mutants; (3) the affinies of the CHI mutations for MgADP are similar to those of the ND mutants; (4) diazoxide potentiates the stimulatory effects of MgADP on CHI mutants; and (5)

mutations in ABCC8 that result in neonatal diabetes (increased ATP affinity) or hyperinsulinism of infancy (reduced ATP affinity), are associated with opposite changes in ADP affinity and diazoxide sensitivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of neonatal diabetes mellitus (NDM) and congenital hyperinsulism (CHI).
the regulation of the ATP-sensitive K(+-) channel (KATP channel) by the sulfonylureas.
how nucleotides regulate KATP channels, and how mutations in the channel subunits cause disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ATP/ADP balance in the cell determines whether KATP channels are open or closed and that the ATP/ ADP balance is determined by the relative affinities of the channel subunits for ATP and AD P.
mutations that increase ATP affinity cause ND and mutations that decrease ATP affinity cause CHI.
the ATP-sensitive K(±) channels are regulated by the balance of ATP and ADP concentrations and that this balance is altered in the disease states of neonatal diabetes and congenital hyperinsulism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mutations in ABCC8 that cause neonatal diabetes have increased affinity for MgATPo and those that cause congenital hyperinsulism have reduced affinity.
the clinical phenotypes of ND and CHIs caused by ABCC8 mutations are related to their relative affinities for MgATP.
ND mutations are associated with increased ATP affinity and reduced ADP affinity, while CHI mutations show the opposite effect, increased ADP affinity and reduced ATP affinity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the clinical phenotypes associated with ABCC8 mutations in the NBD2 and TMD2 domains can be explained by their affinities (K(D) values) for MgATP, and that these values can be used to predict the clinical phenotypes of ABCC8 mutations.
ND and CHI are caused by different mechanisms, and that the CHI phenotype is not simply due to a loss-of-function in the channel.
mutations that increase ATP affinity for SUR1 cause neonatal diabetes, whereas those that reduce affinity cause hyperinsulinism.
